prompt: Feed these decoded characters to the line editor in order: `a`, `b`, `c`, Backspace, Ctrl+U, Backspace, `x`, Ctrl+C, Enter. Echo rules: printable = 1 byte, backspace = `"\b \b"` (3 bytes) only if there is something to delete, Ctrl+U = 3 bytes per removed character, Ctrl+C = `"^C\r\n"`, Enter = `"\r\n"`. How many echo bytes in total have been written after each marked step?

trace.label: [total echo bytes] after Ctrl+U (the line was `ab`)
[total echo bytes] after the Backspace on the now empty line

explain: a, b, c echo 3 bytes and the Backspace adds `\b \b` = 3, so 6 (buffer `ab`). Ctrl+U removes two characters, one `\b \b` each = 6 more, 12. Backspace on an empty line echoes nothing, otherwise the cursor would eat the prompt: still 12. `x` is 1 byte and Ctrl+C prints `^C\r\n` = 4 bytes, so 17. Enter adds `\r\n` = 2 for 19. The echo must always mirror the buffer, which is why ignored input is not echoed.
